Week01-AssignmentA-AI-Game-Jam.md.title: AI in Classic Games
Week01-AssignmentA-AI-Game-Jam.md.summary: The assignment involves writing a paper on a game significantly influenced by AI developments. The chosen game should be old enough to have evolved through various computer systems, like Chess, Go, Pong, or Pac-Man. The essay should cover the game's historical context, current state, and potential AI-driven future.

Week01-AssignmentB-History-Timeline.md.title: Algorithm History Timeline
Week01-AssignmentB-History-Timeline.md.summary: The assignment requires students to create a timeline detailing the history of algorithms, mathematics, statistics, artificial intelligence, or machine learning. Using a specified GitHub tool, students are guided to focus on significant figures, concepts, or eras in these fields, incorporating multimedia elements for enhanced understanding. The work should be completed and published as a GitHub page.

Week01-LectureA-Introduction-To-AI.md.title: Introduction to AI
Week01-LectureA-Introduction-To-AI.md.summary: The document introduces Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a field focused on enabling computers to exhibit intelligent behavior in tasks that are difficult to explicitly program, like estimating a person's age from a photograph. It distinguishes between Weak AI, which is specialized in specific tasks, and Strong AI, which refers to systems capable of human-like intelligence, also known as Artificial General Intelligence.

Week01-LectureB-History-Of-Machine-Learn.title: Machine Learning History
Week01-LectureB-History-Of-Machine-Learn.summary: The lecture explores key historical milestones in the development of machine learning and artificial intelligence, emphasizing their intertwined nature and shared intellectual origins. Key discoveries discussed include Bayes Theorem, Least Square Theory, Markov Chains, and the Perceptron, all of which have significantly contributed to the evolution of these fields.

Week02-AssignmentA-Build-An-Ontology.md.title: Ontology Building Task
Week02-AssignmentA-Build-An-Ontology.md.summary: The assignment involves creating a knowledge base by constructing an ontology for a chosen topic, such as a person, place, or object. Participants are to utilize techniques and strategies from the lesson to differentiate between similar entities, for example, distinguishing between rooms in a house. The task includes using the Protégé application to build the ontology.

Week02-LabA-Animal-Expert-System.ipynb.title: Animal Expert System Implementation
Week02-LabA-Animal-Expert-System.ipynb.summary: This Jupyter Notebook implements a simple knowledge-based Animal Expert System using an AND-OR tree structure. It defines a custom language for knowledge representation with Python classes, enabling backward inference to determine animals based on their physical characteristics. The system includes classes like `Ask`, `If`, `AND`, and `OR` to model questions and rules.

Week02-LabB-Family-Ontology.ipynb.title: Family Relationships Ontology Analysis
Week02-LabB-Family-Ontology.ipynb.summary: The Jupyter Notebook titled 'Week02-LabB-Family-Ontology' is part of the AI for Beginners Curriculum and demonstrates the use of ontologies to define and infer family relationships using the Romanov Tsar Family's genealogical data in GEDCOM format. It utilizes the 'python-gedcom' library for parsing GEDCOM files to extract and display individual and family data, showcasing how to manipulate and analyze genealogical information programmatically.

Week02-LabC-Concept-Graph.ipynb.title: Semantic Relationships with ConceptNet
Week02-LabC-Concept-Graph.ipynb.summary: This Jupyter Notebook demonstrates how to use the ConceptNet API to explore semantic relationships, specifically `IsA` relations, between concepts. It includes a Python function to query the ConceptNet API and retrieve related concepts with calculated weights. Additionally, it mentions integrating news categorization using the NewsApi.org service. The notebook replaces the outdated Microsoft Concept Graph API with ConceptNet, a freely available semantic network.

Week02-LectureA-Knowledge-Representation.title: Knowledge Representation
Week02-LectureA-Knowledge-Representation.summary: The lecture discusses the foundational concepts in symbolic AI, focusing on knowledge representation and reasoning. It explains the difference between data, information, and knowledge, highlighting that knowledge is an actively developed understanding of the world through integrating information. The content also introduces the DIKW Pyramid, which illustrates how data transforms into knowledge through interpretation and integration.

Week03-AssignmentA-Get-Up-And-Running.md.title: Python Setup Assignment
Week03-AssignmentA-Get-Up-And-Running.md.summary: This non-graded assignment focuses on setting up your environment for running Python notebooks, and brushing up on Python programming skills. It suggests completing a Python learning path and watching introductory setup videos. The goal is to ensure you are prepared for future machine learning exercises.

Week03-AssignmentB-Interview-A-Data-Scie.title: Data Scientist Interview
Week03-AssignmentB-Interview-A-Data-Scie.summary: The assignment involves interviewing a professional data scientist to understand their daily responsibilities, focusing on whether they are specialists or work across the full data science stack. A 500-word essay documenting the findings is required, evaluated on length and proper source attribution.

Week03-AssignmentC-Regression-Model.md.title: Regression Model Assignment
Week03-AssignmentC-Regression-Model.md.summary: The assignment involves creating a regression model using Linear or Polynomial Regression techniques. A dataset should be chosen, either from Scikit-learn's built-in sets or another source. The notebook must include an explanation of the chosen technique and an assessment of the model's accuracy. The rubric evaluates the completeness, documentation, and functionality of the solution.

Week03-LectureA-Introduction-To-Machine-.title: Machine Learning Introduction
Week03-LectureA-Introduction-To-Machine-.summary: This beginner's course introduces classical machine learning, providing resources to set up your computer and learn essential programming languages like Python and JavaScript. You'll need tools like Python, Node.js, and a text editor for development, as well as a GitHub account to fork the curriculum. The course also references Scikit-learn, an ML library, for practical learning.

Week03-LectureB-Techniques-Of-Machine-Le.title: Machine Learning Techniques
Week03-LectureB-Techniques-Of-Machine-Le.summary: The machine learning process involves several key steps: defining a predictive question, gathering and preparing relevant data, selecting an appropriate training method, training the model with algorithms to recognize data patterns, and evaluating the model's performance. These steps require specific expertise and involve experimentation with various techniques to optimize the model's accuracy.

Week03-LectureC-Linear-Regression.md.title: Linear Regression Techniques
Week03-LectureC-Linear-Regression.md.summary: This lesson introduces linear regression techniques using Scikit-learn, focusing on predicting numerical outcomes like pumpkin prices. It explains basic and polynomial regression methods with minimal mathematical prerequisites. The lesson involves training models to predict data outcomes, building on the visualization of the pumpkin pricing dataset. Pre-cleaned data and Jupyter notebooks facilitate hands-on learning.

Week04-AssignmentA-Multi-Class-Perceptro.title: Perceptron Multi-Class Classifier
Week04-AssignmentA-Multi-Class-Perceptro.summary: This assignment involves extending a binary classification model for MNIST handwritten digits into a multi-class classifier. The task requires training ten perceptrons, each distinguishing a specific digit from the others. Combining their weights enables simultaneous predictions across all digits, with accuracy computed and a confusion matrix generated for evaluation.

Week04-LabA-Perceptron.ipynb.title: Perceptron Binary Classification Implementation
Week04-LabA-Perceptron.ipynb.summary: The Jupyter Notebook focuses on implementing a perceptron algorithm for binary classification problems, using a toy dataset to classify data points into positive or negative classes. It imports necessary libraries, generates a synthetic dataset with two features, and prepares the data for training and testing by converting labels and splitting the dataset. Additionally, it includes initial setup for plotting the data.

Week04-LabB-Multi-Class-Perceptron.ipynb.title: Multi-Class Perceptron Lab Assignment
Week04-LabB-Multi-Class-Perceptron.ipynb.summary: The Jupyter Notebook 'Week04-LabB-Multi-Class-Perceptron.ipynb' provides a practical lab assignment for training a perceptron on a multi-class classification task. It includes importing necessary libraries, defining a perceptron training function, and a function to measure accuracy. Additionally, it outlines the task of loading a dataset for training and evaluation purposes, catering to beginners in AI.

Week04-LectureA-Introduction-To-Neural-N.title: Introduction to Neural Networks
Week04-LectureA-Introduction-To-Neural-N.summary: The document introduces neural networks as mathematical models inspired by the brain to achieve artificial intelligence. Neural networks are a subset of machine learning, focused on using data for training models capable of solving problems like classification and regression. The curriculum emphasizes neural network models while recommending a separate resource for classical machine learning.

Week04-LectureB-Perceptron.md.title: Perceptron Neural Network
Week04-LectureB-Perceptron.md.summary: The perceptron, developed in 1957, is an early neural network model designed for binary classification, distinguishing between two classes of input data. It uses a single neuron and a step activation function to compute outputs based on input features. Training involves adjusting weights to minimize classification errors.

Week05-AssignmentA-MNIST-With-Own-Framew.title: MNIST Neural Network Lab
Week05-AssignmentA-MNIST-With-Own-Framew.summary: This lab assignment involves classifying MNIST handwritten digits using 1-, 2-, and 3-layered perceptrons within a custom neural network framework. Participants are expected to explore how activation functions and network layers affect performance and training dynamics, including the behavior of weights over epochs. Additional guidance is provided through a starting notebook.

Week05-AssignmentB-Classification-With-F.title: Neural Network Classification
Week05-AssignmentB-Classification-With-F.summary: This lab assignment involves solving two classification problems using neural networks with PyTorch or TensorFlow. The first task is to classify iris flowers into three categories using tabular data, and the second task is to classify handwritten digits from the MNIST dataset. Participants are encouraged to experiment with different network architectures to maximize accuracy.

Week05-LabA-Own-Framework.ipynb.title: Custom Neural Framework Development
Week05-LabA-Own-Framework.ipynb.summary: This Jupyter Notebook is part of Microsoft’s AI for Beginners curriculum and is designed to guide users in building their own neural framework for solving classification and regression tasks using multi-layered perceptrons. It begins with setting up a sample dataset using Python libraries, and includes steps to visualize and analyze this data using custom plots.

Week05-LabB-MNIST-With-Own-Framework.ipy.title: MNIST Classification with Custom Framework
Week05-LabB-MNIST-With-Own-Framework.ipy.summary: This lab notebook guides users through downloading and preparing the MNIST dataset for digit classification using a custom neural network framework. It involves splitting the dataset, defining models with varying perceptron layers, and analyzing how different activation functions and network complexities impact model performance.

Week05-LabC-Intro-To-PyTorch.ipynb.title: Introduction to PyTorch Framework
Week05-LabC-Intro-To-PyTorch.ipynb.summary: The Jupyter Notebook introduces PyTorch, a neural network framework from Facebook, highlighting its capabilities such as tensor operations on various compute units and automatic gradient computation. It also contrasts PyTorch with other popular frameworks, like Tensorflow and Keras, and provides basic installation instructions. Readers are guided to check their PyTorch version to ensure they are working with a recent release.

Week05-LabD-Intro-To-Keras-And-TensorFlo.title: Intro to TensorFlow and Keras
Week05-LabD-Intro-To-Keras-And-TensorFlo.summary: This Jupyter Notebook provides an introduction to TensorFlow and Keras, explaining their roles in implementing neural networks. It outlines the capabilities of these frameworks, including tensor operations and gradient computation, and discusses popular frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch. The notebook also ensures that users have the appropriate TensorFlow version installed and briefly introduces the concept of tensors.

Week05-LabE-Frameworks-Classification.ip.title: Iris Classification with Python Libraries
Week05-LabE-Frameworks-Classification.ip.summary: This Jupyter Notebook is part of a lab assignment focused on classification using frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow. It utilizes the Iris Dataset from Scikit Learn to demonstrate data preparation and visualization, including feature extraction and pairwise plotting with Seaborn. The lab emphasizes dataset normalization and encoding as preliminary steps for neural network modeling.

Week05-LectureA-Multi-Layered-Perceptron.title: Advanced Neural Networks
Week05-LectureA-Multi-Layered-Perceptron.summary: This section builds on the previous introduction of a one-layered perceptron by extending it to handle more complex tasks such as multi-class classification and regression. It discusses constructing a modular neural network framework in Python, covers formalizing machine learning problems, and emphasizes various loss functions for different tasks. The text also touches on converting outputs to probabilities using techniques like softmax.

Week05-LectureB-Frameworks-And-Overfitti.title: Neural Network Frameworks
Week05-LectureB-Frameworks-And-Overfitti.summary: Neural network frameworks need to efficiently compute tensor operations and gradients, enabling GPU computation. TensorFlow and PyTorch offer low-level APIs with support for these tasks, while Keras and PyTorch Lightning provide high-level APIs.

Week06-AssignmentA-Explore-The-RAI-Toolb.title: Responsible AI Exploration
Week06-AssignmentA-Explore-The-RAI-Toolb.summary: The assignment involves exploring a notebook from the Responsible AI Toolbox to analyze and improve AI systems, with a focus on fairness. Participants are required to present a paper or presentation detailing their findings, including the systems explored and conclusions reached.

Week06-LectureA-Responsible-AI.md.title: Ethical AI
Week06-LectureA-Responsible-AI.md.summary: The lecture discusses the ethical use of AI, highlighting that AI, though powerful, is just a tool that can be misused. It emphasizes the importance of responsible AI, focusing on principles like fairness to address biases in data and models, ensuring ethical deployment and usage.

Week06-LectureB-Fairness-In-Machine-Lear.title: Responsible AI in ML
Week06-LectureB-Fairness-In-Machine-Lear.summary: This lesson introduces the impact of machine learning in daily life decisions and emphasizes the importance of fairness and accountability in AI systems. Key topics include assessing demographics in data, exploring outliers, protecting privacy, and ensuring system inclusivity and transparency. The curriculum aims to build trust and safety into AI applications.
